catalog_quote: Ang stress ay isang phonemic na suprasegmental; ang posisyon nito ay nakapagbabago ng kahulugan ng salita. Karaniwang nasa ultima at penultima ang stress ngunit hindi predictable ang paglalagay nito. 2.2.1.1 Ultima /lɪ'mʌ/ ‘lima; five’ /Ɂʊ'tʊt/ ‘utot; flatulence’ /gʌlʌ'mʌj/ ‘daliri; finger’ /pʌhɪ'ŋʌ/ ‘palaka; frog’ 2.2.1.2 Penultima /'Ɂʌho/ ‘aso; dog’ /'Ɂʌpʌt/ ‘apat; four /Ɂʌ'hʌwʌ/ ‘asawa; spouse’ /bʊ'wʌtʃɪ/ ‘bulate; worm’ Minimal Pair /da'gɪt/ ‘ningas; to blaze as a fire’ /'dagɪt/ ‘kislap; flash’ /pʊ'hʊɁ/ ‘puso; heart’ /'pʊhʊɁ/ ‘puso ng saging; banana heart’ /tʊ'lʊj/ ‘tuloy; materialize, finalize, take place’ /'tʊlʊj/ ‘tulog; lie down, sleep’ /hʊ'jʊ/ ‘mangaso sa gabi; hunt at night (with flashlight tied to head)’ /'hʊjʊ/ ‘lingkod, silbi ... [sec. 2.5, p. 37:] Ang stress ay phonemic ngunit hindi ang length o haba. ... [p. 38:] Ang stress at length ay walang simbolo sa orthography.

audit.reasoning: (1) The deciding quotation, the minimal pairs, and the sec. 2.5/p. 38 summary lines are all verbatim in the held Endriga & San Juan 2018 chapter at the stated printed pages 28-29, 37, 38. (2) The source is a 2018 university grammar sketch with a dedicated stress section and stress-only minimal pairs; Glottolog's 21-item bibliography and Crossref/SIL searches show no phonology article, acoustic study or fuller grammar for this language, so it is the best available. (3) Independent confirmation fetched sources now: the SIL Philippines online Ayta Mag-antsi dictionary (Storck & Storck) marks stress per entry, with both penult and final stress and a stress-only homograph pair (LA.wak vs la.WAK), matching the 'lexical' coding; Johnson 2006 is silent. Remaining unheld items (Kitano & Pangilinan 2003; print dictionary front matter) are low-priority corroboration, not likely to change the coding. Web se

sources.citation: Storck, Kurt & Margaret Storck (comps.). 2012/2013. Ayta Mag-antsi Dictionary - Pallêkan Habi, online edition (SIL Philippines, published online 12 July 2013; 5178 headwords). https://sil-philippines-languages.org/online/sgb/dict/
sources.quote: No prose statement reachable (intro page 404), but every entry carries a syllabified pronunciation field with the stressed syllable in capitals, and stress position varies by lexeme: penult in A.hê 'no', DI.la 'tongue', KA.nêng, LA.wah 'always', BAN.da; final in al.WA 'don't', pa.AN 'don't', tag.LOH, pang.ga.HAK; and a stress-only homograph pair lawak 1 LA.wak 'plateau of tall grass' vs lawak 2 la.WAK 'drool, salivate'.
